issues.legal_issue: A purchaser at a judicial sale in execution of a decree later reversed is not protected from restitution if the purchaser was the decree-holder, knew of the pending appeal, or colluded with or acted as a name-lender for the decree-holder.
material_facts: A money decree was executed while the judgment debtor’s appeal against it was pending, and the judgment debtor’s properties were sold at a court auction to a person who was not formally a party to the decree.
The decree was later reversed on appeal, and the judgment debtor sought restitution of the properties.

Evidence showed that the auction purchaser was related by marriage to the decree-holder, lacked money of his own to buy the properties, and joined the decree-holder in an agreement to sell one of the properties.
issues.conclusion: The auction purchaser was not a bona fide purchaser, so the sale in his favour had to fall for restitution.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 144 of the Code of Civil Procedure, courts must remedy injury caused by their proceedings and restore parties, so far as possible, to the position they would have occupied absent the decree. A bona fide stranger purchaser without knowledge of the pending litigation is generally protected when the decree is later reversed or modified, as stated in Janak Raj v. Gurdial Singh and Sardar Govindrao Mahadik v. Devi Sahai. That protection does not extend to a decree-holder purchaser, a purchaser who knew of the pending appeal, or a collusive or nominal purchaser. The Court rejected the contrary approach in R. Raghavachari v. M.A. Pakkiri Mahomed Rowther and relied also on Chhota Nagpur Banking Association v. C.T.M. Smith, Jamnomal Gurdinomal v. Gopaldas, Rodger v. The Comptoir D’Escompte De Paris, and A.R. Antulay v. R.S. Nayak. The procedural provisions in Order 21, rules 89–91 do not require courts to protect a purchaser who is not bona fide when restitution is otherwise warranted.

rule.if: execution_sale and decree_later_reversed and (purchaser_is_decree_holder or purchaser_knew_of_pending_appeal or purchaser_colluded_with_decree_holder_or_acted_as_name_lender)

predicates.execution_sale: The property was sold at a judicial sale held to execute a decree.
predicates.decree_later_reversed: The decree under which the sale was held was later reversed or modified.
predicates.purchaser_is_decree_holder: The person who bought the property at the sale was the decree-holder.
predicates.purchaser_knew_of_pending_appeal: The purchaser knew of the pending appeal against the decree when buying the property.
predicates.purchaser_colluded_with_decree_holder_or: The purchaser colluded with the decree-holder or bought the property as the decree-holder’s nominal purchaser.

issues.definition: When a decree is later reversed or modified, restitution is required for property sold in its execution if the purchaser was the decree-holder, knew of the pending appeal, or colluded with or acted as a nominal purchaser for the decree-holder.
